# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hambrick_2026_cefepime"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hambrick_2026_cefepime"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijantimicag.2026.107741>
* Supplement (positive cultures, dosing summary, diagnostic plots): <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijantimicag.2026.107741>, supplementary material
* Base model: `MoralesJunior_2025_cefepime` in this package
  (<https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-025-01485-5>)

Hambrick 2026 asks whether urine neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin
(uNGAL), a marker of real-time tubular injury, predicts cefepime clearance
beyond what serum-creatinine eGFR already explains. The authors took the
validated Morales Junior 2025 PICU cefepime model, held every structural,
variability and residual-error parameter at its published value, re-estimated
only the eGFR exponent, and tested uNGAL in several forms. The retained form is
a binary indicator: an admission uNGAL of 500 ng/mL or more lowers clearance by
a factor of `exp(-0.42) = 0.657`. The authors also added inter-occasion
variability (IOV) on clearance and central volume, with the first 48 h of PICU
admission as occasion 1 and the time thereafter as occasion 2.

# Population

Fifty patients were enrolled at the Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical
Center PICU; one (a patient with paraplegia whose low muscle mass gave a
supra-normal eGFR of about 200 mL/min/1.73 m^2) was excluded, leaving 49
patients and 296 scavenged plasma concentrations (2-11 per patient, median 6;
59% in the first 48 h of PICU admission). Enrolment required a renal angina
index of 8 or more, which triggers a reflex uNGAL order, and cefepime started
within 48 h of PICU admission. Median age was 11.5 years (IQR 5-17, range 3
months to 31 years), median study-day-1 weight 29.4 kg (IQR 20-50) and 50% were
female (Table 1).

Kidney function was impaired on average: median SCr-eGFR on PICU admission
62.2 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (IQR 41-122), with 68% meeting KDIGO creatinine criteria
for AKI on admission (66% stage 2-3). Median admission uNGAL was 154.5 ng/mL
(IQR 118-2065); 15 patients (30%) had uNGAL of 500 ng/mL or more. Illness was
severe: 74% were mechanically ventilated, 66% received vasopressors and the
median number of organ failures was 2. Patients on dialysis or any
extracorporeal therapy at screening were excluded.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Hambrick_2026_cefepime")()$population`.

# Source trace

Per-parameter origins are also recorded as comments next to each `ini()` entry
in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Hambrick_2026_cefepime.R`. Values marked "held"
carry an asterisk in Table 2 and are the Morales Junior 2025 final estimates.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `cl <- exp(lcl + etalcl + iov_cl + e_urine_ngal_cl * (URINE_NGAL >= 500)) * (WT/70)^0.75 * (CRCL/147.6)^e_crcl_cl` | n/a | Table 2 CL equation `CL = CLpop x (WT/70)^0.75 x (eGFR/147.6)^beta x e^(beta_NGAL x NGAL(1 or 0)) x e^etaCl`; threshold 500 ng/mL from Results ("Modelling uNGAL as a binary variable using a threshold of 500 ng/mL yielded the greatest reduction in the OFV") |
| `lcl` | `log(6.38)`, held | Table 2, CLpop 6.38* |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 0.75, held | Table 2 CL and Q equations |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.40 | Table 2, beta eGFR 0.40 (RSE 25.5%; bootstrap 0.22-0.54) |
| `e_urine_ngal_cl` | -0.42 | Table 2, beta NGAL -0.42 (RSE 36.9%; bootstrap -0.76 to -0.13) |
| `vc <- exp(lvc + etalvc + iov_vc) * (WT/70) * exp(0.026 * CUM_FLUID_BAL_PCT)` | n/a | Table 2 V1 equation (exponential fluid-balance form as printed in Morales Junior 2025 Table 2) |
| `lvc` | `log(15)`, held | Table 2, V1pop 15* |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 1, held | Table 2 V1 and V2 equations (bare `(WT/70)`) |
| `e_cum_fluid_bal_pct_vc` | 0.026, held | Table 2, beta Cum%FB 0.026* |
| `lq`, `q <- exp(lq) * (WT/70)^0.75` | `log(3.65)`, held | Table 2, Qpop 3.65* and Q equation |
| `lvp`, `vp <- exp(lvp) * (WT/70)` | `log(8.91)`, held | Table 2, V2pop 8.91* and V2 equation |
| `etalcl` | 0.1355452 (38.1% CV), held | Table 2, IIV CL 38.1%*; footnote CV = sqrt(e^omega^2 - 1) x 100 |
| `etalvc` | 0.0219581 (14.9% CV), held | Table 2, IIV V1 14.9%* |
| `etaiov_cl_1`, `etaiov_cl_2` | 0.0878360 (30.3% CV) | Table 2, IOV CL 30.3% (RSE 16.0%) |
| `etaiov_vc_1`, `etaiov_vc_2` | 0.0199634 (14.2% CV) | Table 2, IOV V1 14.2% (RSE 73.3%) |
| Occasions | 1 = first 48 h of PICU admission, 2 = after | Methods, 'Population pharmacokinetic modelling' |
| `propSd` | 0.319, held | Table 2, error model proportional only, b 31.9%* |
| Unbound fraction 0.80 | outside the model | Methods, 'Monte Carlo simulations' ("We assumed 20% protein binding") |

```{r load-model}
# Two expected messages are muffled, and only these two: random effects are
# passed as data columns with `omega = NA` ("multi-subject simulation without
# 'omega'"), and the IOV etas enter clearance and volume through derived
# occasion terms, which rxode2 reports as "non-mu referenced".
quiet_known <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'|non-mu referenced", conditionMessage(w))) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  })
}
solve_quiet <- function(...) quiet_known(rxode2::rxSolve(...))

ui <- quiet_known(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hambrick_2026_cefepime")))
mod <- ui
```

# Structural verification

These checks are deterministic (no random draws), so their tolerances are
tight.

## Typical values and the uNGAL effect

At 70 kg, eGFR 147.6 mL/min/1.73 m^2, zero fluid balance and uNGAL below 500
ng/mL the model must return the Table 2 population values; at uNGAL of 500
ng/mL or more, clearance must fall by `1 - exp(-0.42)`, the "~35% lower CL" of
the Abstract.

```{r typical-values}
mod_typ <- quiet_known(mod |> rxode2::zeroRe())

typ_events <- tidyr::crossing(
  id = 1:3, time = c(0, 1)
) |>
  mutate(
    evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_,
    WT = 70, CRCL = c(147.6, 147.6, 62.2)[id],
    URINE_NGAL = c(100, 500, 100)[id],
    CUM_FLUID_BAL_PCT = 0, OCC = 1L
  )
typ_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typ_events |> distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 2000, time = 0),
  typ_events
) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

typ_sim <- solve_quiet(mod_typ, typ_events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  distinct(id, cl, vc, q, vp)

typ <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "CL, eGFR 147.6, uNGAL < 500 (L/h)",
    "V1 (L)", "Q (L/h)", "V2 (L)",
    "CL ratio, uNGAL >= 500 vs < 500",
    "CL ratio, eGFR 62.2 vs 147.6"
  ),
  Expected = c(6.38, 15, 3.65, 8.91, exp(-0.42), (62.2 / 147.6)^0.40),
  Model = c(
    typ_sim$cl[1], typ_sim$vc[1], typ_sim$q[1], typ_sim$vp[1],
    typ_sim$cl[2] / typ_sim$cl[1], typ_sim$cl[3] / typ_sim$cl[1]
  )
) |>
  mutate(`% diff` = 100 * (Model - Expected) / Expected)

# Same arithmetic on both sides; only floating-point error remains.
stopifnot(max(abs(typ$`% diff`)) < 1e-8)

knitr::kable(typ, digits = c(0, 4, 4, 10))
```

The threshold is inclusive: a uNGAL of exactly 500 ng/mL takes the lower
clearance, matching the paper's "uNGAL >= 500 ng/mL" wording.

## Occasion switching

The occasion index `OCC` selects which IOV eta applies. With the two IOV etas
supplied as data (+0.2 on occasion 1, -0.2 on occasion 2) and every other
random effect at zero, clearance must be `6.38 * exp(0.2)` on occasion-1
records and `6.38 * exp(-0.2)` on occasion-2 records.

```{r occasion-check}
occ_events <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = c(0, 24, 47, 49, 72), evid = c(1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L),
  amt = c(2000, NA, NA, NA, NA), cmt = "central",
  OCC = c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L), WT = 70, CRCL = 147.6, URINE_NGAL = 100,
  CUM_FLUID_BAL_PCT = 0,
  etalcl = 0, etalvc = 0,
  etaiov_cl_1 = 0.2, etaiov_cl_2 = -0.2, etaiov_vc_1 = 0, etaiov_vc_2 = 0
)
occ_sim <- solve_quiet(mod, occ_events, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame")
occ_cl <- occ_sim |>
  mutate(OCC = ifelse(time < 48, 1L, 2L)) |>
  group_by(OCC) |>
  summarise(cl = unique(cl))
stopifnot(
  abs(occ_cl$cl[1] / (6.38 * exp(0.2)) - 1) < 1e-8,
  abs(occ_cl$cl[2] / (6.38 * exp(-0.2)) - 1) < 1e-8
)
knitr::kable(occ_cl, digits = 4)
```

## Variability round-trips through the Table 2 footnote

```{r variability-roundtrip}
om <- ui$omega
cv <- tibble::tibble(
  Eta = c("etalcl", "etalvc", "etaiov_cl_1", "etaiov_vc_1"),
  `Published CV (%)` = c(38.1, 14.9, 30.3, 14.2),
  `Model CV (%)` = 100 * sqrt(exp(diag(om)[Eta]) - 1)
)
# Stored variances are rounded to seven decimals.
stopifnot(max(abs(cv$`Model CV (%)` - cv$`Published CV (%)`)) < 1e-3)
knitr::kable(cv, digits = 4)
```

# Virtual cohort

The cohort follows the Monte Carlo design of the Methods ('Monte Carlo
simulations'): body weight uniform on 5-40 kg (weight-based dosing) or 40-100
kg (fixed dosing), eGFR uniform within 30-60, 60-90 or 90-150
mL/min/1.73 m^2, uNGAL placed on one side of the 500 ng/mL threshold, and
cumulative fluid balance 0% for everyone. That gives twelve cells; each holds
200 virtual patients, and the same patients are re-used under every regimen so
regimen comparisons are paired.

Covariates and random effects are drawn with base R's random-number generator
and passed to `rxSolve()` as data columns (`omega = NA`), so the cohort is the
same on every machine and at every solver thread count. Only the occasion-1 IOV
etas are drawn: the paper evaluates target attainment at 48 h, inside occasion
1. The main replication sets the IOV etas to zero, because that is what
reproduces the published tables (see 'Inter-occasion variability in the Monte
Carlo simulations' below); the IOV draws are kept for the sensitivity analysis.

```{r cohort}
n_per_cell <- 200L
set.seed(20260521)

cells <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  band = c("5-40 kg", "40-100 kg"),
  egfr = c("30-60", "60-90", "90-150"),
  ngal = c(">= 500", "< 500")
)
egfr_lim <- list("30-60" = c(30, 60), "60-90" = c(60, 90), "90-150" = c(90, 150))
wt_lim <- list("5-40 kg" = c(5, 40), "40-100 kg" = c(40, 100))
sd_eta <- sqrt(diag(om))

cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(k) {
  tibble::tibble(
    band = cells$band[k],
    egfr = cells$egfr[k],
    ngal = cells$ngal[k],
    WT = stats::runif(n_per_cell, wt_lim[[cells$band[k]]][1], wt_lim[[cells$band[k]]][2]),
    CRCL = stats::runif(n_per_cell, egfr_lim[[cells$egfr[k]]][1], egfr_lim[[cells$egfr[k]]][2]),
    URINE_NGAL = if (cells$ngal[k] == ">= 500") 1000 else 100,
    CUM_FLUID_BAL_PCT = 0,
    OCC = 1L,
    etalcl = stats::rnorm(n_per_cell, 0, sd_eta[["etalcl"]]),
    etalvc = stats::rnorm(n_per_cell, 0, sd_eta[["etalvc"]]),
    iov_cl_draw = stats::rnorm(n_per_cell, 0, sd_eta[["etaiov_cl_1"]]),
    iov_vc_draw = stats::rnorm(n_per_cell, 0, sd_eta[["etaiov_vc_1"]])
  )
})) |>
  mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(), etaiov_cl_2 = 0, etaiov_vc_2 = 0)

stopifnot(nrow(cohort) == 12L * n_per_cell, !anyDuplicated(cohort$id))

cohort |>
  group_by(band, egfr) |>
  summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    `WT median (kg)` = median(WT),
    `eGFR median` = median(CRCL),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort by weight band and eGFR stratum (both uNGAL groups).")
```

# Simulation

The six regimens of Tables 3 and 4: 50 mg/kg (maximum 2000 mg) every 12 or 8 h
as a 30-min standard infusion (SI) or 3-h extended infusion (EI), and 100 or 150
mg/kg/day (maximum 4000 / 6000 mg/day) as a continuous infusion (CI). The
40-100 kg cohort receives the fixed caps (2000 mg per dose, 4000 or 6000
mg/day). Dosing starts at time 0 and target attainment is read off the dosing
interval that ends at 48 h.

```{r simulate}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,   ~ii, ~dur, ~per_kg, ~cap,
  "q12h SI",   12,  0.5,      50, 2000,
  "q12h EI",   12,  3.0,      50, 2000,
  "q8h SI",     8,  0.5,      50, 2000,
  "q8h EI",     8,  3.0,      50, 2000,
  "100 mg/kg/d CI", 24, 24,  100, 4000,
  "150 mg/kg/d CI", 24, 24,  150, 6000
)

simulate_regimen <- function(k, coh) {
  ii <- regimens$ii[k]
  coh <- coh |>
    mutate(amt = ifelse(band == "5-40 kg", pmin(regimens$per_kg[k] * WT, regimens$cap[k]), regimens$cap[k]))
  dose <- coh |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 48 - ii, by = ii)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dur = regimens$dur[k])
  obs <- coh |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = seq(48 - ii, 48, by = 0.1)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_)
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
  solve_quiet(mod, ev, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame", keep = c("band", "egfr", "ngal")) |>
    mutate(regimen = regimens$regimen[k])
}

cohort_main <- cohort |> mutate(etaiov_cl_1 = 0, etaiov_vc_1 = 0)
sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), simulate_regimen, coh = cohort_main))

stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))
```

## Concentration profiles

```{r profiles}
sim |>
  filter(band == "5-40 kg", regimen == "q8h SI") |>
  group_by(egfr, ngal, time) |>
  summarise(Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50, colour = ngal, fill = ngal)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 8 / 0.8, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~egfr, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Total plasma cefepime (mg/L)",
    colour = "uNGAL (ng/mL)", fill = "uNGAL (ng/mL)",
    title = "50 mg/kg q8h over 30 min, 5-40 kg, dosing interval ending at 48 h",
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles. Dotted line: total concentration equal to free 8 mg/L at fu = 0.80."
  )
```

At every eGFR stratum the uNGAL >= 500 ng/mL group sits higher, because its
clearance is 34% lower.

## Clearance against eGFR and uNGAL

Figure 1 of the paper plots individual clearance from the base model (before
uNGAL was added) against admission uNGAL; the individual estimates are not
public. The panel below shows the relationship the final model encodes: typical
weight-normalised clearance against eGFR, for each uNGAL group, with the
paper's 3.75 L/h/70 kg^0.75 reference line.

```{r figure-1-analogue}
cl_curve <- tidyr::crossing(CRCL = seq(30, 200, by = 2), URINE_NGAL = c(100, 1000)) |>
  mutate(
    cl70 = 6.38 * (CRCL / 147.6)^0.40 * exp(-0.42 * (URINE_NGAL >= 500)),
    group = ifelse(URINE_NGAL >= 500, ">= 500", "< 500")
  )
ggplot(cl_curve, aes(CRCL, cl70, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3.75, linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(
    x = "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)", y = "Typical CL (L/h per 70 kg^0.75)",
    colour = "uNGAL (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Model-side counterpart of Figure 1 of Hambrick 2026 (typical values, no random effects)."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. The check below runs PKNCA on a steady-state (`ss =
1`) solve of the 5-40 kg cohort under 50 mg/kg q8h SI, grouped by uNGAL group
and eGFR stratum, and compares the interval AUC against the exact steady-state
identity `AUC0-tau = Dose / CL` computed from each subject's own clearance.

```{r pknca}
nca_coh <- cohort_main |>
  filter(band == "5-40 kg") |>
  mutate(group = paste0("eGFR ", egfr, ", uNGAL ", ngal), amt = pmin(50 * WT, 2000))

ss_dose <- nca_coh |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dur = 0.5, ii = 8, ss = 1L)
ss_obs <- nca_coh |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 8, by = 0.02)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, ii = NA_real_, ss = NA_integer_)
ss_sim <- solve_quiet(
  mod, dplyr::bind_rows(ss_dose, ss_obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid)),
  omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "group", maxsteps = 1e6
)

conc_df <- ss_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, group)
conc_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  conc_df,
  conc_df |> distinct(id, group) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = NA_real_)
) |>
  distinct(id, group, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | group + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  nca_coh |> mutate(time = 0) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, group),
  amt ~ time | group + id,
  doseu = "mg"
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 8, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)
stopifnot(nrow(nca_tbl) > 0)
```

## AUC0-tau against the closed form

```{r auc-closed-form}
auc_chk <- nca_tbl |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))) |>
  dplyr::select(id, group, auc_nca = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(ss_sim |> distinct(id, cl), by = "id") |>
  left_join(nca_coh |> dplyr::select(id, amt), by = "id") |>
  mutate(auc_closed = amt / cl, pct_diff = 100 * (auc_nca - auc_closed) / auc_closed)

stopifnot(nrow(auc_chk) == nrow(nca_coh), !anyNA(auc_chk$pct_diff))
# Same drawn parameters on both sides, so the difference is trapezoidal error on
# a 0.02-h grid plus LSODA tolerance (realised max about 0.01%). 1% still
# catches a mis-encoded dose cap, infusion duration or unit.
stopifnot(max(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 1)

reference <- auc_chk |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(auclast = median(auc_closed), .groups = "drop")

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = reference,
  by = "group",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Steady-state AUC0-8 from PKNCA vs the exact Dose/CL reference, 50 mg/kg q8h SI, 5-40 kg. * differs by >20%."
)
```

No row is starred. Exposure summary by group:

```{r nca-summary}
nca_tbl |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "cav", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin,
    "Cavg (mg/L)" = cav,
    "AUC0-8 (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median steady-state NCA, 50 mg/kg q8h SI, 5-40 kg.")
```

# Probability of target attainment (Tables 3 and 4)

The target is 100% fT > MIC: the free concentration (0.80 x total) stays above
the MIC for the whole dosing interval ending at 48 h. MICs of 2, 8 and 32 mg/L
cover 1x and 4x the 2025 CLSI breakpoints for Enterobacterales (2 mg/L) and
*Pseudomonas aeruginosa* (8 mg/L).

```{r pta}
fu <- 0.80
cmin_48 <- function(s) {
  s |>
    group_by(band, egfr, ngal, regimen, id) |>
    summarise(fcmin = min(fu * Cc), .groups = "drop")
}
pta_from <- function(cm) {
  cm |>
    tidyr::crossing(MIC = c(2, 8, 32)) |>
    group_by(band, egfr, ngal, regimen, MIC) |>
    summarise(pta = 100 * mean(fcmin > MIC), .groups = "drop")
}
pta <- pta_from(cmin_48(sim))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~band, ~egfr, ~regimen, ~h2, ~h8, ~h32, ~l2, ~l8, ~l32,
  "5-40 kg", "30-60", "q12h SI", 98.8, 87.8, 36.8, 90.3, 56.8, 8.7,
  "5-40 kg", "30-60", "q12h EI", 99.5, 92.4, 44.4, 94.6, 66.7, 12.2,
  "5-40 kg", "30-60", "q8h SI", 100, 98.3, 73.3, 99, 87.7, 35.1,
  "5-40 kg", "30-60", "q8h EI", 100, 99.5, 82.7, 99.8, 94, 46.7,
  "5-40 kg", "30-60", "100 mg/kg/d CI", 100, 100, 95.7, 100, 100, 76.5,
  "5-40 kg", "30-60", "150 mg/kg/d CI", 100, 100, 99.7, 100, 100, 95.4,
  "5-40 kg", "60-90", "q12h SI", 96.4, 75.2, 19.2, 79.5, 36.7, 2.8,

# The 40-100 kg CI regimens are fixed 4000 and 6000 mg/day in Table 4.
pta_cmp <- pta |>
  inner_join(published, by = c("band", "egfr", "regimen", "ngal", "MIC")) |>
  mutate(diff = pta - published)
stopifnot(nrow(pta_cmp) == 216L)
```

## Table 3: 5-40 kg, weight-based dosing

```{r table-3}
t3 <- pta_cmp |> filter(band == "5-40 kg")

t3 |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", pta, published)) |>
  dplyr::select(egfr, regimen, ngal, MIC, cell) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(ngal, MIC), values_from = cell, names_glue = "uNGAL {ngal}, MIC {MIC}") |>
  dplyr::rename("eGFR" = egfr, "Regimen" = regimen) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PTA (%) for 100% fT > MIC, simulated (published Table 3 in brackets).")

# Cells strictly between 2% and 98% carry information; the saturated ones agree
# trivially. With 200 patients per cell the Monte Carlo SE of a PTA near 50% is
# 3.5 points. Realised: median diff -0.5, 90th percentile |diff| 6.5 (an
# independent 200-per-cell cohort, scored on the cells with published PTA
# between 5% and 95%, gave -0.6 / 5.0). A mis-transcribed
# clearance, eGFR exponent or uNGAL coefficient shifts these cells by 10-30
# points.
t3_inf <- t3 |> filter(published > 2, published < 98)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(t3_inf$diff)) < 4,
  quantile(abs(t3_inf$diff), 0.9) < 12
)
```

Simulated attainment reproduces Table 3: across the
`r nrow(t3_inf)` informative cells the median difference is
`r sprintf("%.1f", median(t3_inf$diff))` percentage points and the 90th
percentile of the absolute difference is
`r sprintf("%.1f", quantile(abs(t3_inf$diff), 0.9))` points, about what 200
patients per cell allow.

## Table 4: 40-100 kg, fixed dosing

```{r table-4}
t4 <- pta_cmp |> filter(band == "40-100 kg")

t4 |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", pta, published)) |>
  dplyr::select(egfr, regimen, ngal, MIC, cell) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(ngal, MIC), values_from = cell, names_glue = "uNGAL {ngal}, MIC {MIC}") |>
  dplyr::rename("eGFR" = egfr, "Regimen" = regimen) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PTA (%) for 100% fT > MIC, simulated (published Table 4 in brackets).")

t4_inf <- t4 |> filter(published > 2, published < 98)
t4_q8_ci <- t4_inf |> filter(!grepl("^q12h", regimen))
t4_q12 <- t4_inf |> filter(grepl("^q12h", regimen))
# q8h and continuous-infusion rows: same tolerance as Table 3.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(t4_q8_ci$diff)) < 4,
  quantile(abs(t4_q8_ci$diff), 0.9) < 12
)
```

The q8h and continuous-infusion rows of Table 4 agree as closely as Table 3
(median difference `r sprintf("%.1f", median(t4_q8_ci$diff))` points). The
**q12h rows do not**: the simulated q12h attainment is a median
`r sprintf("%.1f", -median(t4_q12$diff))` points below the published value.
Table 4 itself shows why: its q12h and q8h rows are nearly identical (for
example 99.1% vs 99.2% at eGFR 30-60, uNGAL >= 500, MIC 8), although giving the
same 2000 mg dose every 12 h instead of every 8 h must lower the trough. The
published q12h rows instead match a q8h simulation:

```{r table-4-q12h}
q8_as_q12 <- pta |>
  filter(band == "40-100 kg", grepl("^q8h", regimen)) |>
  mutate(regimen = sub("q8h", "q12h", regimen)) |>
  inner_join(published, by = c("band", "egfr", "regimen", "ngal", "MIC")) |>
  mutate(diff = pta - published)

q12_compare <- t4_q12 |>
  dplyr::select(egfr, regimen, ngal, MIC, published, q12h_sim = pta) |>
  left_join(
    q8_as_q12 |> dplyr::select(egfr, regimen, ngal, MIC, q8h_sim = pta),
    by = c("egfr", "regimen", "ngal", "MIC")
  )

q12_compare |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "eGFR" = egfr, "Regimen (as labelled)" = regimen, "uNGAL" = ngal,
    "Published" = published, "Simulated q12h" = q12h_sim, "Simulated q8h" = q8h_sim
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Table 4 'q12h' rows against q12h and q8h simulations, informative cells.")

# The published q12h rows sit with the q8h simulation and far from the q12h one.
# Realised: median |q8h - published| 2.6, median (q12h - published) -26.5.
q8_fit <- q12_compare |> filter(!(egfr == "30-60" & ngal == "< 500" & MIC == 32 & grepl("SI", regimen)))
stopifnot(
  median(abs(q8_fit$q8h_sim - q8_fit$published)) < 5,
  median(q12_compare$q12h_sim - q12_compare$published) < -10
)
```

The one exception is the eGFR 30-60, uNGAL < 500, MIC 32 mg/L cell of the 2000
mg q12h SI row, which reads 90.9%, the same as the MIC 8 mg/L cell beside it and
far above the 36.6% of the q12h EI row below it; it is treated as a copy error
and excluded from the check. Table S2's adult recommendations of 2000 mg q12h
rest on the q12h rows, so they inherit the problem. None of this touches the
model parameters, which come from Table 2.

## Inter-occasion variability in the Monte Carlo simulations

The packaged model carries the Table 2 IOV. The paper does not say whether its
Simulx runs sampled it. Adding the occasion-1 IOV draws widens the clearance
distribution (total log-scale variance on CL rises from 0.136 to 0.223), and
the simulated attainment then falls below Table 3 in the informative cells:

```{r iov-sensitivity}
cohort_iov <- cohort |>
  filter(band == "5-40 kg") |>
  mutate(etaiov_cl_1 = iov_cl_draw, etaiov_vc_1 = iov_vc_draw)
sim_iov <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), simulate_regimen, coh = cohort_iov))
pta_iov <- pta_from(cmin_48(sim_iov)) |>
  inner_join(published, by = c("band", "egfr", "regimen", "ngal", "MIC")) |>
  filter(published > 2, published < 98) |>
  mutate(diff = pta - published)

iov_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  Simulation = c("IIV only", "IIV + IOV"),
  `Median diff (points)` = c(median(t3_inf$diff), median(pta_iov$diff)),
  `90th pct |diff| (points)` = c(quantile(abs(t3_inf$diff), 0.9), quantile(abs(pta_iov$diff), 0.9))
)
knitr::kable(iov_summary, digits = 1, caption = "Table 3 informative cells, simulated minus published PTA.")
```

The IIV-only simulation centres on the published values, while adding IOV
pulls attainment down by about two points in the median (an independent
cohort, scored on the cells with published PTA between 5% and 95%, gave -0.6
without and -2.8 with IOV), so the published tables were most likely generated
without IOV. Use IIV only to reproduce the paper's
dosing tables; include IOV (the default when `rxSolve()` samples the model's
omega) to describe a patient's variability across the two PICU periods.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **uNGAL as a continuous column.** The model takes the measured admission
  uNGAL (`URINE_NGAL`, ng/mL) and applies the 500 ng/mL threshold inside
  `model()`. The threshold is inclusive (`>=`), as the paper writes it. Any
  value on the correct side of 500 gives the same result; the cohort above uses
  1000 and 100 ng/mL.
* **V1 equation.** The Table 2 V1 row is typeset as `V1pop x (WT/70) x beta x
  Cum%FB x e^etaV1`, which drops the exponential. The exponential form
  `exp(0.026 x Cum%FB)` is taken from the Morales Junior 2025 Table 2 equation,
  whose value Hambrick 2026 holds; Hambrick's text describes the model as
  "cumulative fluid balance as a covariate on central volume" without changing
  its form. The Monte Carlo design sets fluid balance to 0%, so the
  replication does not test this term.
* **Held parameters.** Every value with an asterisk in Table 2 is encoded with
  `fixed()`, since the authors did not estimate it in this fit. Only the eGFR
  exponent, the uNGAL coefficient and the two IOV variances are estimates of
  Hambrick 2026.
* **Occasions.** Occasion 1 is the first 48 h after PICU admission and
  occasion 2 everything after (Methods). The clock is PICU admission, not the
  first cefepime dose, which could precede admission by up to 48 h; users must
  build `OCC` from admission time. The two occasions share one variance per
  parameter, encoded as a free occasion-1 variance and a `fixed()` occasion-2
  copy.
* **Abstract typo.** The Abstract says IOV "at 4 h post-PICU admission"; the
  Methods, Results and Discussion all give 48 h, which is used.
* **Monte Carlo set-up.** The paper reports "simulated concentration-time
  profiles at 48 h" without more detail. Here dosing starts at time 0 and 100%
  fT > MIC is evaluated over the dosing interval ending at 48 h (the whole
  24-48 h day for continuous infusion), on the individual predictions without
  residual error. Cohorts are 200 patients per cell rather than 10 000.
* **IOV not in the replication.** See the sensitivity section above: the
  published PTA tables are reproduced without IOV.
* **Table 4 q12h rows.** The published 40-100 kg q12h rows match a q8h
  simulation, and one cell (eGFR 30-60, uNGAL < 500, MIC 32, q12h SI = 90.9%)
  duplicates its neighbour. This is documented above and does not affect the
  model.
* **Unbound fraction.** Free concentration is 0.80 x total, the paper's
  assumed 20% protein binding; it is not part of the model.
* **Scope.** The model must not be used for patients on dialysis, CRRT, ECMO
  or plasma exchange (excluded), or for anuric patients, who cannot provide
  uNGAL. The authors note the model has not been externally validated and that
  predictions for high-normal kidney function rest partly on extrapolation.
